title: Splitting generic irreducible components over an irreducible finite etale model
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and suppose $S$ is nonempty and irreducible (any two nonempty open subsets intersect). There exist a nonempty open subscheme $U\subseteq S$, a nonempty irreducible affine scheme $B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and a finite etale surjective morphism $g:B\to U$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] such that every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of the scheme-theoretic generic fibre $P_\xi$ of $P=X\times_S B\to B$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-scheme-fibre], where $\xi$ is the generic point of $B$ [def-sc-generic-point], is geometrically irreducible over $\kappa(\xi)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]: its inverse image after every field extension is nonempty and irreducible. The generic fibre is allowed to be empty. There is no Noetherian, reducedness, separatedness or flatness hypothesis on $S$ or $f$.

proof.text: Choose a point of the nonempty base and a nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ through it by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. This open is irreducible: two of its nonempty opens are nonempty opens of $S$ and intersect. By [lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime], the nilradical $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ is prime. In the Zariski topology its closure is $V(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Spec}A$, since every prime contains every nilpotent element. Thus $\mathfrak p$ is the generic point of $V$. Put $K=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $Y=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$, with the canonical residue-field point through $V$. Finite-type base change [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] makes $Y/K$ finite type.

Apply [lem-sbc-generic-components-split] to $Y/K$. Obtain $L/K$ with finite etale spectrum map and all components of $Y_L$ geometrically irreducible, in the explicit inverse-image sense of the item. The affine definition of finiteness [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] says that $L$ is a finite $K$-module. At the unique point of each field spectrum, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-residue-field-extension-separable] says that this same field extension is separable algebraic. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-primitive-element] gives $\alpha\in L$ with $L=K(\alpha)$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-residue-polynomial-lift] to $A,\mathfrak p,L,\alpha$. Obtain $c\notin\mathfrak p$ and a monic $F\in A[T]$ whose image in $K[T]$ is the minimal polynomial of $\beta=\bar c\alpha$. Since $\bar c\ne0$, $K(\beta)=K(\alpha)=L$. Put $d=\deg F\ge1$ and $D=A[T]/(F)$. The degree agrees with that of its image: the leading coefficient is $1$ and remains nonzero in $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], $D$ is finite free on $1,t,\ldots,t^{d-1}$. By [lem-sfb-monic-quotient-faithful-tensor-coordinates], $A\to D$ is faithfully flat, hence flat. Thus $h:\operatorname{Spec}D\to V$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine], finite by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-ring-map-finite], and locally of finite presentation by its displayed one-generator one-relation presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

The fibre of $h$ at $\mathfrak p$ is affine: finite base change and the affine-target assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] apply. Its section algebra is $D\otimes_AK$ by [lem-sbc-affine-fibre-sections-tensor]. There is a $K$-algebra isomorphism $D\otimes_AK\simeq K[T]/(\bar F)\simeq L$. For the first map, send $t\otimes1$ to $T$ and $1\otimes k$ to $k$; the inverse sends a polynomial class to its evaluation at $t\otimes1$, and the relations on each side make both composites identities. For the second, evaluate at $\beta$. Evaluation is onto since $K[\beta]=L$ (the finite-dimensional subalgebra generated by an algebraic element is a field); division by the monic minimal polynomial shows its kernel is $(\bar F)$, since a nonzero remainder of smaller degree cannot vanish. Consequently $h_{\mathfrak p}\simeq\operatorname{Spec}L$ over $K$. In particular the set-theoretic fibre consists of a single point $q$, by [def-pc-scheme-fibre].

The fibre in Step 4 is etale: its structure map is precisely the finite etale field-spectrum map of Step 2. Apply [lem-sbc-flat-fibre-etale-neighbourhoods] to $h$, with flatness and local finite presentation supplied in Step 3. Obtain an open neighbourhood $W$ of the sole fibre point $q$ such that $W\to V$ is etale. The closed-map assertion [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] makes $Z=h(\operatorname{Spec}D\setminus W)$ closed in $V$. It misses $\mathfrak p$, since $q\in W$ is its only preimage. Choose an affine open $U$ with $\mathfrak p\in U\subseteq V\setminus Z$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. This is a nonempty open of $S$.

Set $B=h^{-1}(U)$ with its open subscheme structure, and let $g:B\to U$ be the restriction. It is the base change of the finite morphism $h$, hence finite; since $U$ is affine, $B$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence]. By the definition of $Z$, $B\subseteq W$. Thus $B=W\times_VU$ (both are the same restricted open subscheme), and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] makes $g$ etale. The image $g(B)$ is closed in $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. It contains $\mathfrak p$. Every closed subset of $U$ containing this point is all of $U$, since its closure in $V$ is $V$. Therefore $g$ is surjective, and $B$ is nonempty.

The point $q$ remains the sole preimage of $\mathfrak p$ in $B$. For every nonempty open $O\subseteq B$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] makes $g(O)$ a nonempty open of $U$. Such an open contains $\mathfrak p$: a closed complement containing the generic point would contain its whole closure. Hence $q\in O$. Thus $\overline{\{q\}}=B$, and $q$ is generic [def-sc-generic-point]. The closure of a singleton is irreducible: if covered by two closed subsets, one contains the singleton and therefore its closure. It follows that $B$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components]. This uses no reducedness and does not claim that the coordinate ring of $B$ is a domain.

The identification in Step 4 also gives $\kappa_B(q)=L$ compatibly with $K\to L$. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies the local ring at $q$ before and after restriction to $B$ with $D_q$. Localizing the fibre algebra $D\otimes_AK=L$ at its unique prime gives $D_q/\mathfrak pD_q=L$. Since this quotient is a field, $\mathfrak pD_q$ is the maximal ideal of the local ring $D_q$; its residue field is therefore $L$ by [def-weil-residue-field]. The maps from $A$ in these quotient/localization identifications are the original maps, so the residue-field point $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_B(q)\to B\to S$ is the given composite $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$.

Put $P=X\times_SB$ and $\xi=q$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and the compatible residue-field map in Step 8, its generic fibre is isomorphic over $L$ to $Y_L$. Explicitly, both $(X\times_SB)\times_B\operatorname{Spec}L$ and $(X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K)\times_K\operatorname{Spec}L$ represent a map to $X$ and a map to $\operatorname{Spec}L$ agreeing in $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The maps preserving these projections are inverse by uniqueness. After any extension $E/L$ the same construction gives the compatible isomorphism of $E$-fibres. Isomorphisms give homeomorphisms, which preserve maximal irreducible subsets [def-weil-irreducible-components], and the commuting projections identify their inverse images after extension. Step 2 therefore gives precisely nonempty irreducibility of each such inverse image. If $Y$ is empty, both generic fibres are empty and the component assertion is vacuous. The cover constructed above still exists, including when $L=K$ and $d=1$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_etale_irreducible_generic_component_splitting {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IrreducibleSpace S] (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] : ∃ U : S.Opens, (U : Set S).Nonempty ∧ ∃ B : Scheme.{u}, IrreducibleSpace B ∧ IsAffine B ∧ ∃ g : B ⟶ U.toScheme, IsFinite g ∧ Etale g ∧ Surjective g ∧ ∃ ξ : B, IsGenericPoint ξ Set.univ ∧ ∀ A ∈ irreducibleComponents ↥((pullback.snd f (g ≫ U.ι)).fiber ξ), ∀ (E : Type u) (_ : Field E) (z : Spec (CommRingCat.of E) ⟶ Spec (B.residueField ξ)), IsIrreducible ((pullback.fst ((pullback.snd f (g ≫ U.ι)).fiberToSpecResidueField ξ) z) ⁻¹' A)
